title: A Phase 2 Study of Dynamic BH3 Profiling (DBP) Guided Combination Therapy in Subjects With R/R AML
official: A Phase 2 Study Using the Dynamic BH3 Profiling Assay to Guide Venetoclax-Based Combination Therapy for Participants With Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia
summary: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of using the dynamic BH3 profiling (DBP) assay as a biomarker to guide venetoclax-based combination therapy for participants with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Willing to undergo a bone marrow aspirate for biomarker testing.
* Participants must have a diagnosis by WHO 2006 of one of the following:

  * Participants with Relapsed AML must have at least 5% morphologic marrow blasts to be eligible. Extramedullary disease allowed but marrow involvement required.
  * Participants with Refractory AML are defined as those without a complete remission after two courses (or cycles) of any remission-induction regimen (intensive chemotherapy or less intensive regimen such as hypomethylating agent-venetoclax based treatment or low-dose cytarabine agent-venetoclax based treatment).
  * Participants with Secondary AML arising out of a previously treated prior myeloid neoplasm treated with intensive chemotherapy or at least two cycles of HMA/venetoclax-based treatment.
  * Participants may also be Relapsed/Refractory.
* ECOG performance status ≤ 2 (see Appendix A)
* Participants decline, must not be eligible or are not recommended by treating provider to receive immediate allogeneic transplantation or available FDA-approved AML regimens.
* Participants must meet the following organ function as defined below:

  * total bilirubin ≤ 3 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN) unless considered to be due to leukemic organ involvement or Gilbert's disease. For participants with Gilbert's syndrome, participants may enroll if direct bilirubin ≤ 3xULN
  * AST(SGOT) and ALT(SGPT) ≤ 3 × institutional ULN
  * Creatinine clearance ≥ 30mL/min using Cockroft Gault formula
* If male, even if surgically sterilized (i.e., status post-vasectomy), participant must agree to use adequate barrier contraception prior to the study, for the duration of study participation, and 6 months after completion of study drug administration, or agree to practice true abstinence, when this is in line with the preferred and usual lifestyle of the participant. (Periodic abstinence \[e.g., calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, postovulation methods for the female partner\] withdrawal, spermicides only, and lactational amenorrhea are not acceptable methods of contraception.)
* If female, participant must be either:

  * Postmenopausal (surgically sterile or age \> 55 years with no menses for 12 or more months without an alternative medical cause or age 55 or less with no menses for 12 or more months without an alternative medical cause AND an FSH level \>40 IU/L) or
  * Women of childbearing potential must agree to use adequate contraception (defined as 1 highly effective method \[hormonal\] and 1 additional effective \[barrier\] method of birth control at the same time) 30 days prior to study entry, for the duration of study participation, and through 6 months after the last dose of study drug or agree to practice true abstinence when this is in line with the preferred and usual lifestyle of the participant. Female and male condoms should not be used together. Periodic abstinence (e.g., calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post ovulation methods), withdrawal, spermicides only, and lactational amenorrhea are not acceptable methods of contraception.
  * Women of childbearing potential: Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while she or her partner is participating in this study, she should inform her treating physician immediately.
  * Women of childbearing potential: Participant must have a negative serum beta-HCG test result (local labs are allowed) at screening. Repeat testing is required within 72 hours prior to first study dose (local labs are allowed).
* White blood cell count \< 25,000/L prior to first dose on study protocol treatment. Hydroxyurea or leukapheresis are permitted to meet this criterion (hydroxyurea may be resumed after biomarker collection takes place).
* Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.
* For combination venetoclax, azacitidine, and tagraxofusp assignment, must also meet the following organ function criteria:

  * Creatinine clearance (measured by Cockcroft-Gault formula or measured by 24-hour urine collection) ≥ 45 mL/minute; participants between 18 and 74 years of age may have creatinine clearance ≥ 30 mL/minute
  * Albumin \> 3.2 g/dL (administration of albumin is permitted to achieve albumin eligibility if the baseline serum albumin is ≥ 3.0g/dL)
  * Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) except in participants with Gilbert's syndrome. Participants with Gilbert's syndrome may enroll if direct bilirubin ≤ 3 x ULN of the direct bilirubin.
* For combination venetoclax, azacitidine, and revumenib assignment, must also meet the following organ function criteria:
* Total bilirubin ≤ 2.0 x upper limit of normal (ULN) except in participants with Gilbert's syndrome. Participants with Gilbert's syndrome may enroll if direct bilirubin ≤ 3.0 x ULN of the direct bilirubin.

Exclusion Criteria:

* During biomarker collection: For purpose of dynamic BH3 profiling assay (biomarker) to optimize cell viability, participants must not be on any anti-leukemic therapy for at least 5 days prior to bone marrow aspirate collection with the exception of hydroxyurea which must be held at least 48 hours prior to aspirate collection. Note: hydroxyurea use is allowed immediately after bone marrow aspirate collection if clinically indicated.
* Participants who have had chemotherapy (with exception of hydroxyurea and/or dexamethasone which are allowed) or radiotherapy or investigational therapy within 5 half-lives or 14 days (whichever is shorter) prior to starting treatment on study.
* More than two prior AML-directed salvage regimens defined as any line of therapy given for a relapsed or refractory indication (excluding initial induction regimen, allogeneic transplant, donor lymphocyte infusion, hydroxyurea, cytarabine for cytoreduction purposes).
* Venetoclax within 14 days prior to starting treatment on study.
* Any prior investigational therapy-related AEs must be grade 1 or at baseline prior to first dose on study (except for alopecia).
* Has known acute promyelocytic leukemia.
* Concurrent use of medications that are moderate or strong CYP450 inducers within 7 days of first dose on study. Because the lists of these agents are constantly changing, it is important to regularly consult a frequently-updated medical reference. As part of the enrollment/informed consent procedures, the participant will be counseled on the risk of interactions with other agents, and what to do if new medications need to be prescribed or if the participant is considering a new over-the-counter medicine or herbal product. Please consult FDA website as appropriate: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-interactions-labeling/drug-development-and-drug-interactions-table-substrates-inhibitors-and-inducers
* Consumption of grapefruit or grapefruit products, Seville oranges, or star fruit within 3 days prior to first dose on study.
* Participants diagnosed with another malignancy that have either received treatment within 2 years prior to first dose on study or are currently recommended to receive treatment (indicating this other malignancy is active). Exceptions include 1) participants with nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of any type are not excluded if they have undergone resection, 2) previous malignancy confined and surgically resected (or treated with other modalities) with curative intent are allowed, 3) any breast, reproductive or prostate cancer that is well controlled with hormonal or topical therapies.
* Major surgery within 14 days before first dose of any study drug.
* Participants with known, active and uncontrolled heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV), clinically significant arrhythmia, symptomatic cardiomyopathy, unstable angina or myocardial ischemia infarction within last 6 months, and clinically significant pulmonary hypertension requiring pharmacologic therapy. Clinically significant arrhythmia is defined as having one of the following: history of polymorphic ventricular fibrillation or torsade de pointes, permanent atrial fibrillation (continuous for ≥ 6 months), persistent atrial fibrillation (sustained and lasting \> 7 days and/or requiring cardioversion in the 4 weeks before screening), and grade 3 atrial fibrillation (symptomatic and incompletely controlled medically in the past 6 months). Participants with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation or \< Gr 3 atrial fibrillation for period of at least 6 months are permitted to enroll provided that their rate is controlled on a stable regimen if medically indicated.
* History of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to any assigned study agents.
* Known allergy to both xanthine oxidase inhibitors and rasburicase.
* Known HIV seropositive. HIV testing is not required.
* Participants with known, active chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Exception: Participants with undetectable HBV load by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), without liver-related complications, and on definitive HBV therapy are eligible for study. Serologic evidence of prior vaccination is sufficient to participate in the trial (vaccination however is not required for trial).
* Participants with known chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection requiring treatment. However, if a participant with a history of HCV infection has received definitive therapy (and is now HCV viral load negative), or if a participant has a reactive HCV antibody test but has an undetectable viral load by PCR, then he/she would be eligible.
* Immediate life-threatening, severe complications of leukemia such as uncontrolled bleeding, respiratory failure, or coagulopathy.
* Symptomatic or (known) active CNS involvement of AML. Prophylactic intra-thecal chemotherapy is permitted.
* Participants with active or uncontrolled infection at time of first dose of treatment on study. Prophylaxis is allowed. Participants receiving anti-microbial agents including antibiotics, antiviral or antifungal therapies are allowed if hemodynamically stable and afebrile for 72 hours (unless fever is thought to be from underlying leukemia).
* Other severe acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition or laboratory abnormality that in the opinion of the investigator may increase the risk associated with study participation or investigational product administration or may interfere with the interpretation of study results and/or would make the participant inappropriate for enrollment into this study.
* Vaccination with live, attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks prior to initiation of study treatment or anticipation of need for such a vaccine during the study. (COVID19 vaccinations are allowed.)
* Malabsorption syndrome or other clinically significant condition (including difficulty swallowing oral medications) that would preclude enteral administration.
* Female participants who are lactating and breastfeeding, intention to participate in IVF (in vitro fertilization), or intending to donate eggs (ova) during course of this trial or 6 months after receiving last dose of study drug.
* Male participants who intend to donate sperm during the course of this study or 6 months after receiving their last dose of study drug(s).
* Participants assigned to combination venetoclax and gilteritinib are excluded with the following: Heart rate corrected QT interval (QTcF) ≥ 500 msec or with other factors that increase the risk of QT prolongation or arrhythmic events (e.g., heart failure, hypokalemia, family history of long QT interval syndrome).
* Participants assigned to combination venetoclax, azacitidine, and tagraxofusp are excluded with any clinically significant cardiac disease or abnormalities defined as:

  * LVEF is less than lower limit of normal by MUGA scan or echocardiogram.
  * Myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or evidence of poorly controlled atrial fibrillation leading to a complication or severely symptomatic such that daily activity is affected within 12 months prior to first dose on study.
  * Any history of congenital long QT syndrome sustained ventricular tachycardia requiring intervention, ventricular fibrillation, or torsades de pointes.
  * Presence at screening of second- or third-degree AV block without a permanent pacemaker, bi-fascicular block (right bundle branch block \[RBBB\] with left anterior hemiblock), or complete left bundle branch block.
  * QTc using Fridericia's correction (QTcF) \>480 msec. Triplicate ECG requested for tagraxofusp at screening.
* Participants assigned to combination venetoclax, azacitidine, and revumenib are excluded with the following:

  * Participants \<40 kg in weight.
  * Concurrent use of moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers (prohibited)
  * LVEF is \<50% by MUGA scan or echocardiogram,
  * QTc using Fridericia's correction (QTcF) \>450 msec,
  * History of acute pancreatitis within 6 months of first dose on study or history of chronic pancreatitis,
  * Known cirrhosis with a Child-Pugh score of B or C.
  * Known personal or family history of long QT syndrome.
  * Required use of QT-prolonging agents (except for those with low risk for QT prolongation and used as standard supportive medications e.g. famotidine, Bactrim, azoles, anti-emetics, antibacterial agents such as levofloxacin, ciprofloxacin or azithromycin, diphenhydramine).
  * Any of the following within 6 months before first dose on study: myocardial infarction, uncontrolled/unstable angina, congestive heart failure (NYHA Class ≥II), life-threatening uncontrolled arrhythmia, cerebrovascular accident, or transient ischemic attack. Participants with controlled atrial fibrillation are allowed to enroll.
